questions.prompt: In a sources and uses table, which item is typically the 'plug'?
questions.explanation: Lenders set how much debt they will provide, and the sponsor funds whatever remains. Equity is the balancing figure.

questions.prompt: Which of these belongs in 'uses' but is most often left out of a careless model?
choices: The purchase price of the equity
Transaction fees, which can run to several percent of enterprise value
questions.explanation: Fees are paid at closing from the same pot as the purchase price, so every rupee of fees is sponsor equity that bought nothing. Omitting them flatters the model.

questions.prompt: Why can the same company support meaningfully different leverage in two different years?
choices: Because EBITDA is recalculated under different accounting standards
Because lenders set the ceiling, and their appetite moves with the credit cycle
Because sponsor equity requirements are set by regulation
Because management rollover changes the enterprise value
questions.explanation: The constraint is what lenders will accept on leverage and coverage tests, and that moves with credit conditions — which is why buyout vintages perform so differently.

questions.prompt: Management rollover exists mainly to reduce the amount of equity the sponsor must contribute.
questions.explanation: False. Its purpose is alignment. A management team with most of its net worth in the equity behaves differently over the holding period from one that has cashed out entirely.

questions.prompt: Walk through what belongs on each side of a sources and uses table for a buyout, and explain why the target's existing debt appears in uses and its cash appears in sources.
rubric: Lists the main uses: purchase of equity, refinancing existing debt, transaction fees, and cash left on the balance sheet
Lists the main sources: senior secured debt, subordinated or high-yield debt, sponsor equity, management rollover, and target cash
Explains that existing debt usually becomes repayable on a change of control, so it must be funded at closing
Explains that the target's cash is available to fund the transaction, reducing what must be raised
States that sources must equal uses and that sponsor equity is the balancing figure
